hypotheses: settled Copper/Gold state may add incremental context for distinguishing mid-cycle pullback from terminal distribution
decision-relevant value must survive Jan-Feb versus Feb-Mar anchor sensitivity
component decomposition may reveal whether ratio movement is copper-led or gold-led

prospective_outcomes.primary_question: Does the challenger improve recoverable-pullback versus terminal-distribution discrimination over the baseline?

negative_controls: best single component Copper or Gold

kill_criteria.K01: source identity or units become ambiguous
kill_criteria.K02: lookahead or incomplete-bar use is required to retain apparent edge
kill_criteria.K03: decision-relevant conclusion depends on one 2M anchor only
kill_criteria.K04: no incremental divergence from baseline after prospective maturation
kill_criteria.K06: threshold tuning against known BTC tops becomes necessary
kill_criteria.K07: small-N prevents useful discrimination after sufficient prospective time
kill_criteria.K08: source freshness, units, schema, duplicate or continuity validation fails
kill_criteria.K09: source revisions cannot be reproduced through payload hash and immutable revision receipt
kill_criteria.K16: containment: candidate is structurally contained by an existing retained composite or information family
kill_criteria.K17: numeric evidence cannot be reproduced through deterministic parsing and exact provenance

minimum_evaluation_sample: at least 12 settled observations per anchor and at least two independent crypto transition episodes

historical_prior.finding: All five objective terminal proxies were EXPANSION or ACCELERATING at the BTC peak; simple deterioration was not an early terminal warning.
